title.justification: The title 'The Termination Critic' is explicitly stated at the beginning of the abstract.

analysis.description: This paper focuses on autonomously discovering behavioral abstractions, or options, for reinforcement learning agents by proposing an algorithm that centers on the termination condition instead of the policy. It introduces a critic, which is the option transition model that guides the termination condition, leading to an algorithm that learns meaningful terminations that are useful for planning and learning.

type.justification: The paper presents a novel theoretical framework for autonomously discovering options in reinforcement learning by introducing an information-theoretic objective for termination conditions.
type.quote: In this work, we adopt the view that abstractions are primarily useful due to their ability to compress information, which yields speedups in learning and planning.

name.justification: The paper discusses the problem in the context of autonomously discovering options for reinforcement learning agents, introducing a new method for learning terminations in reinforcement learning.
name.quote: Autonomous discovery of meaningful behavioral abstractions in reinforcement learning has proven to be surprisingly elusive.

name.justification: The paper deals with the discovery of options and hierarchies in reinforcement learning, which directly relates to hierarchical reinforcement learning.
name.quote: The option-critic [Bacon et al., 2017] focuses on options [Sutton et al., 1999] as the formal framework of temporal abstraction.

name.justification: ACTC is introduced as the novel algorithm developed in the paper to learn termination conditions using the proposed theoretical framework.
name.quote: We then formalize the proposed objective, express it via the option model, and use the termination gradient result to obtain the online actor-critic termination-critic (ACTC) algorithm.

is_executed.quote: Finally, we empirically study the learning dynamics of our algorithm, the relationship of the proposed loss to planning performance, and analyze the resulting options qualitatively and quantitatively.
